items.summary: 【开源自荐】PTP 时间同步技术书——从思想实验到动手实现 开源地址： 项目简介： 一本开源技术书，从思想实验讲起，深入 PTP/IEEE 1588 协议机制和 LinuxPTP 源码分析，附带一套可运行的 ptplite 教学实现（约 1000 行 C），可在两台 Linux 机器上实际做主从时钟同步。 为什么这很重要？ 自动驾驶需要多传感器（激光雷达、摄像头、IMU）在微秒级对齐时间戳——时间不同步等于传感器白装。PTP/gPTP（IEEE 1588 / 802.1AS）是实现车载时钟同步的核心标准，已广泛应用于主流自动驾驶平台。然而，系统性、从零讲起的中文 PTP 技术资料几乎空白。 运行效果： 核心特性： 📖 41 节 —— 4 个章节覆盖思想实验、协议机制、源码分析、动手实现 🔬 逐机制拆解 —— BMCA 选举、4 个时间戳的数学、透明时钟、PI 伺服控制器 ⚙️ ptplite —— 一个完整的主从时钟实现，可在真实网卡上运行做时间同步 📊 市场验证 —— CSDN 3 周 3 万阅读、1000+ 点赞收藏 开源协议：CC BYNCND 4.0（内容） · MIT（代码）

items.content:
# 〖工具自荐〗SkillDock —— AI Coding 工具的 Skills、MCP 与插件管理台

## 介绍

SkillDock 是一个面向 AI Coding 工具的 macOS 桌面管理工具，用来统一管理本地的 Skills、MCP Servers 和插件包。

它可以把 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Windsurf、Gemini CLI、GitHub Copilot 等工具里分散的配置能力集中起来，支持安装、查看、编辑、同步和更新，减少手动复制文件、修改配置和检查路径的成本。

项目地址：https://github.com/wanghuan9/skill-manager

![SkillDock skills list](https://github.com/wanghuan9/skill-manager/raw/main/docs/images/skill_list.png)

## 特点

- **统一管理 Skills**：集中查看、安装、编辑、删除和同步本地 skills。
- **统一管理 MCP Servers**：支持扫描导入、编辑配置、探测 tools，并按工具启用或停用。
- **支持插件包管理**：插件可以包含 skills、commands、agents、MCP 集成和宿主工具能力。
- **Git-aware 工作流**：Git 来源的 skills 和插件保留真实仓库结构，可检测远端更新、本地修改和待推送状态。
- **多工具一键同步**：同一套 skills、MCP 和插件可以同步到多个 AI Coding 工具。
- **面向团队协作**：发布者可以本地修改后一键推送，使用者可以查看更新内容后一键更新。

## 核心能力

### Skills 管理

SkillDock 会按来源展示已安装的 skills，并保留每个 skill 的来源信息、Git 状态和工具启用状态。

适合团队维护一组公共 skills，然后让不同成员按需同步到 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Windsurf 等工具中。

### MCP 管理

MCP Servers 和 skills 放在同一个工作台中管理。SkillDock 可以扫描本机已有配置，也可以从市场安装 MCP server。

它不仅保存配置，还会尝试探测 MCP server 是否可用，以及暴露了哪些 tools。

![SkillDock MCP detail](https://github.com/wanghuan9/skill-manager/raw/main/docs/images/mcp_detail.png)

### 插件管理

SkillDock 也支持更高层级的插件包管理。一个插件可以包含 skills、commands、agents、MCP 集成和不同宿主工具的扩展能力。

这适合把一组 AI Coding 能力打包分发，而不是只管理单个 skill 或单个 MCP server。

![SkillDock plugin detail](https://github.com/wanghuan9/skill-manager/raw/main/docs/images/plugin_detail.png)

### Git 协作状态

对于从 Git 仓库安装的 skills 和插件，SkillDock 会保留真实仓库结构，而不是简单复制文件。

这样可以继续检测：

- 是否有远端更新
- 本地是否修改过
- 是否有待推送内容
- 更新或推送前具体会变更什么

这对团队维护内部 skills 比较有用，因为 skills 不再只是一次性复制到本地的文件，而是可以持续更新和协作的资产。

## 支持的工具

目前支持或计划支持的工具包括：

Claude Code、Codex、Cursor、Windsurf、IntelliJ IDEA、OpenCode、Gemini、GitHub Copilot、Continue、Qwen Code、Trae、Cline、Roo Code、Kilo Code、Kiro、Goose、Augment、CodeBuddy 等。

## 适用场景

- 同时使用多个 AI Coding 工具
- 想集中管理 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 等工具的 skills
- 想减少 MCP server 手动配置成本
- 团队内部有一批自维护 skills，需要分发、更新和回推
- 希望把 AI Coding 配置从个人零散目录整理成可维护资产

## 总结

SkillDock 不是一个新的 AI 编程助手，而是一个 AI Coding 能力管理工具。

它关注的是 AI Coding 工具进入日常使用以后，skills、MCP servers 和插件越来越多、越来越分散、越来越难维护的问题。通过统一安装、同步、探测和 Git 状态管理，希望让这些能力更容易复用，也更适合团队长期维护。

当前 SkillDock 已支持 macOS，Windows 计划后续支持。源码目前还没有正式开放，仓库先作为公开预览和下载入口，后续功能、文档和发布流程稳定后会考虑开源。

items.title: [投稿] Turn your notes into a practice test: a faster way to study than re-reading
items.author: send2terry
items.summary: Most of us study by rereading. You go over the notes, highlight a few lines, feel like it's sinking in, and then blank on half of it during the exam. The uncomfortable truth from decades of memory research is that rereading is one of the least effective things you can do with your time. It feels productive because the material gets familiar — but familiarity isn't the same as being able to recall it when no one's showing you the answer. The technique that consistently beats rereading is active recall: instead of putting information back into your head, you practice pulling it out. Close the notes and try to answer a question. The moment of effortful retrieval — even when you get it wrong — is what actually strengthens the memory. Selftesting reliably outperforms rereading and highlighting in study after study, and it has a useful side effect: it tells you exactly what you don't know yet, instead of letting you fool yourself. The catch has always been the friction. Writing your own practice questions is tedious, and by the time you've written them you've halfmemorized the answers anyway. Flashcards help but take forever to make. So most people skip the testing and go back to the comfortable, ineffective reread. Here's the workflow I've settled on that removes the friction: 1. Dump your material in. Paste your lecture notes, a chapter of text, or even a PDF of the slides. You don't need to clean it up first. 2. Generate a quiz from it. I use Quiz Maker for this — paste a topic, your notes, or a PDF and it writes a set of questions with an answer key. Multiple choice, true/false, or mixed. It's free and doesn't make you create an account just to try it, which is the whole reason I started using it instead of the tools that gate everything behind a signup. 3. Take the quiz cold. No notes open. The point is to fail a few — that's the signal of where to focus. 4. Restudy only what you missed, then regenerate or retake. This is the loop that actually moves the needle. Autogenerated questions are a starting point, not gospel — skim them and delete or edit any that are ambiguous or test trivia instead of understanding (you can edit every question before you use it). items.content:
Most of us study by re-reading. You go over the notes, highlight a few lines, feel like it's sinking in, and then blank on half of it during the exam. The uncomfortable truth from decades of memory research is that re-reading is one of the least effective things you can do with your time. It feels productive because the material gets *familiar* — but familiarity isn't the same as being able to recall it when no one's showing you the answer.

The technique that consistently beats re-reading is **active recall**: instead of putting information back into your head, you practice pulling it out. Close the notes and try to answer a question. The moment of effortful retrieval — even when you get it wrong — is what actually strengthens the memory. Self-testing reliably outperforms re-reading and highlighting in study after study, and it has a useful side effect: it tells you exactly what you don't know yet, instead of letting you fool yourself.

The catch has always been the friction. Writing your own practice questions is tedious, and by the time you've written them you've half-memorized the answers anyway. Flashcards help but take forever to make. So most people skip the testing and go back to the comfortable, ineffective re-read.

Here's the workflow I've settled on that removes the friction:

1. **Dump your material in.** Paste your lecture notes, a chapter of text, or even a PDF of the slides. You don't need to clean it up first.
2. **Generate a quiz from it.** I use [Quiz Maker](https://quiz-maker.net) for this — paste a topic, your notes, or a PDF and it writes a set of questions with an answer key. Multiple choice, true/false, or mixed. It's free and doesn't make you create an account just to try it, which is the whole reason I started using it instead of the tools that gate everything behind a signup.
3. **Take the quiz cold.** No notes open. The point is to fail a few — that's the signal of where to focus.
4. **Re-study only what you missed,** then regenerate or retake. This is the loop that actually moves the needle.

A few honest caveats. Auto-generated questions are a starting point, not gospel — skim them and delete or edit any that are ambiguous or test trivia instead of understanding (you can edit every question before you use it). For conceptual subjects like math proofs or essay-based humanities, question generation works less well than it does for fact-dense material like biology, history, or vocabulary. And the goal isn't to generate a thousand questions; it's to test yourself, find the gaps, and close them.

The meta-point is simple: the best study method is the one you'll actually do, and "re-reading" wins by default only because making practice questions used to be a chore. Take the chore out and active recall becomes the path of least resistance. That's the entire trick.

*(If you want to try the workflow: paste a topic or your notes at https://quiz-maker.net — no signup to generate.)*

items.author: kestiny18
items.summary: 项目地址： 一句话介绍：面向 Spring Cloud 项目的零配置、只读 Nacos MCP server——把它指向你的项目仓库，自动从 application / bootstrap 文件发现所有环境（dev/test/pre/prod），AI 编程工具（Cursor / Claude Code 等）就能直接查询、搜索、跨环境对比 Nacos 配置。 解决的痛点：维护微服务的同学每周都要回答"这个配置在 dev 和 test 一致吗"——开两个 Nacos 控制台、来回登录、肉眼 diff。现在直接问 AI 一句话，它会自动调工具完成跨环境 key 级对比并给出结论。 特点： 零配置：不需要配任何 host/port/namespace/token，连接信息直接从项目自己的配置文件解析（支持 yml/yaml/properties、多文档 YAML、${} 占位符） 跨环境 diff：内置 nacosdiffconfig 工具，一次调用返回两个环境的结构化差异 只读设计：代码里只有 GET 和登录请求，不存在写操作路径；可选敏感值脱敏 单文件零依赖：纯 Python 标准库实现，内网机器拷一个文件就能用 AI 安装友好：自带 llmsinstall.md，对 Cursor 说一句"帮我装这个 MCP"即可自动完成安装和验证 和官方 nacosmcpserver（单集群、手动配置）是互补关系：官方连集群，这个懂项目。 Apache2.0，带完整测试和 CI，已在真实生产项目（6 模块、4 环境）上验证。
items.content:
**项目地址**：https://github.com/kestiny18/spring-nacos-mcp

**一句话介绍**：面向 Spring Cloud 项目的零配置、只读 Nacos MCP server——把它指向你的项目仓库，自动从 `application-*` / `bootstrap-*` 文件发现所有环境（dev/test/pre/prod），AI 编程工具（Cursor / Claude Code 等）就能直接查询、搜索、跨环境对比 Nacos 配置。

**解决的痛点**：维护微服务的同学每周都要回答"这个配置在 dev 和 test 一致吗"——开两个 Nacos 控制台、来回登录、肉眼 diff。现在直接问 AI 一句话，它会自动调工具完成跨环境 key 级对比并给出结论。

**特点**：

- **零配置**：不需要配任何 host/port/namespace/token，连接信息直接从项目自己的配置文件解析（支持 yml/yaml/properties、多文档 YAML、${} 占位符）
- **跨环境 diff**：内置 `nacos_diff_config` 工具，一次调用返回两个环境的结构化差异
- **只读设计**：代码里只有 GET 和登录请求，不存在写操作路径；可选敏感值脱敏
- **单文件零依赖**：纯 Python 标准库实现，内网机器拷一个文件就能用
- **AI 安装友好**：自带 llms-install.md，对 Cursor 说一句"帮我装这个 MCP"即可自动完成安装和验证

和官方 nacos-mcp-server（单集群、手动配置）是互补关系：官方连集群，这个懂项目。

Apache-2.0，带完整测试和 CI，已在真实生产项目（6 模块、4 环境）上验证。

items.content: AI-generated images now look indistinguishable from real photographs — and they're spreading faster than fact-checkers can catch them. TruthLens is a Chrome extension that analyses any image in your browser and tells you in seconds whether it's AI-generated or real. No login. No technical skill. One click. What's live today: → AI image detection at 80%+ accuracy → Works on any image → Works on mobile via your browser — no app download needed → 5 free analyses per day, no account required

items.title: Trackply
items.summary: Stop applying blindly. Let AI do the work.
items.content: Trackply is an AI-powered Job Search Operating System and personal application database. It automatically tracks and organizes every job you apply to. Key Features: • AI Job Hunter - searches multiple boards + target companies • Auto-tailors resumes & writes personalized cover letters • New: Job Hunt Meta Agent – batch process up to 10 jobs • Smart pipeline tracker with notes & interview tracking • Chrome extension for auto-add to dashbard.

items.title: PJQ
items.summary: See how an audience really received any YouTube video
items.content: PJQ reads the comments under any YouTube video and shows how the audience truly received it: sentiment, support vs disagreement, and bot & spam filtering. Public Judgment Quotient.

items.title: takenorfree.com
items.summary: Domain availability checks for humans and AI agents.
items.content: Is your domain taken or free? Instantly check registration status and DNS records via RDAP—the modern, authoritative protocol behind today's WHOIS. Run single lookups, bulk-check hundreds of domains, or upload a CSV for batch validation. Built for founders, marketers, and developers who need fast answers before they commit. Includes an MCP server so AI agents and assistants can check availability, registration data, and DNS records in your workflow. No guessing—just clear taken-or-free results.
